title: platform-standup-2026-03-14
body:
Date: 2026-03-14
Attendees: Priya, Ethan, Maya, Liam, Sara (+ async notes from Anika)
Start: 10:00am PT

Quick summary:
- Focus this week on control plane stability work (config reconciliation + leader election), routing policy rollout for multi-tier capacity, auth token switching for short-lived service tokens, and quota enforcement bugfixes that caused a small set of customers to see 429s incorrectly.
- No major incidents since 03/10; small regression in quota calc tracked in INF-2478.

Notes / Updates by area:

1) Control plane
- What we worked on: Ethan landed the config reconciliation refactor (GH PR #512) and we started running it behind a feature flag for dedicated clusters. Initial smoke tests look okay; reconciliation loop now tolerates transient datastore errors and re-syncs more aggressively after leader changes.
- Remaining risks: leader election still has a rare edge case where two nodes think they are leaders for ~5s after a DB partition. Maya has a mitigation in draft (backoff + fencing token) — needs more tests.
- Next: roll the feature flag to 25% of dedicated clusters on Monday 03/16, monitor reconciliation latencies and error rates. If stable, 100% roll by end of week.
- Tickets: JIRA INF-2410 (config-reconcile refactor) -> in_review, INF-2499 (leader-election fencing) -> in_progress.

2) Routing (control plane -> serving routing policies)
- What we worked on: Routing team finished the policy DSL change to support cost-based routing (weighting by token-cost metric). Integration tests passing locally.
- Rollout plan: feature gated by org; initial rollout to internal test org tomorrow. We need to confirm compatibility with Dedicated autoscaler (Liam to coordinate).
- Observability: added per-route metric 'route.selection.count' and a dashboard tile to see fallback frequency to cheaper model variants.
- Action: Liam to update runbook to include steps for forcing fallback and to add alerts for unexpected spikes in fallback rate (>5% sustained 10m).

3) Auth & Tokens
- What we worked on: Sara implemented short-lived service token path (rotate via KMS) and updated the token minting endpoint. Deployed to staging. Auth cache TTL reduced from 5m -> 30s to speed up revocations.
- Customer impact: none yet in prod; we have a plan to migrate internal services over the next two weeks.
- Risk: increased token validation calls add load to auth-db; we need to watch auth-db RPS and cache hit rates.
- Ticket: INF-2543 (short-lived tokens) -> in_review.

4) Quotas & Rate Limiting
- What we worked on: fixed quota calc bug where combined-subroute quotas were double-counted for some composite routes (caused erroneous 429s). Patch deployed to prod at 03/13 02:00 UTC. Post-deploy saw reduction in customer 429s for affected orgs.
- Monitoring: added a targeted log filter to capture quota decision traces for top 10 orgs. Two orgs still showing occasional 429s during bursty traffic — investigating whether it's actual exceedance or enforcement race.
- Action: Priya to open a small postmortem if we confirm enforcement race. For now, monitoring and a conservative backoff patch scheduled for 03/16.

Cross-team items / unblockers:
- Autoscaler integration: routing team's cost-based routing needs a compatibility check with Dedicated autoscaler; Liam to schedule a quick sync with infra/scale on 03/15.
- Observability sampling: need to increase KV-cache sampling for the next 48h to validate cache-hit assumptions (Ethan to flip).
- SRE: runbook update for leader-election failover (Maya + SRE) due 03/18.

Blockers:
- None blocking current deploys; leader-election fencing tests failing intermittently in CI (Maya investigative).

Action items (owner — due):
- Ethan: Flip config-reconcile feature flag to 25% for dedicated clusters and monitor metrics (due 2026-03-16).
- Maya: Finish fencing token implementation and add integration tests (due 2026-03-18).
- Liam: Sync with infra/scale about autoscaler compatibility for cost-based routing (schedule meeting by 2026-03-15).
- Sara: Monitor auth-db RPS post-token-ttl change; propose mitigations if >10% increase sustained (due 2026-03-16).
- Priya: Prepare postmortem draft if quota enforcement race is confirmed (on discovery).

Open questions / discussion points:
- Do we want to make the token TTL reduction permanent or revert once short-lived tokens fully rolled out? Pros: faster revocation; Cons: extra DB load. Collect analytics after 1 week on staging.
- Fallback policy thresholds: current default is 5% fallback before alerting — should that be tightened for paid tiers? Product should weigh in.

Misc notes / docs referenced:
- Control plane design v2 (Confluence) — link in linked_artifacts.
- INF-2410, INF-2478, INF-2543 (jira tickets)
- GH PR 512 — config-reconcile refactor (code notes in PR)

Wrap / next steps:
- Primary focus this week: get config-reconcile safely rolled out and leader-election fencing tests passing.
- Routing: complete compatibility check with autoscaler and start org-level rollout for cost-based routing.
- Auth: monitor impact of TTL change and finish token path reviews.
- Quotas: validate fix effectiveness for the two problematic orgs; prepare postmortem if needed.

Next standup: 2026-03-16 (Mon) 10:00am PT

---
Notes to self: capture metric names for dashboard (reconciliation.latency.p95, route.selection.count, auth.cache.hit_rate, quota.decision.trace) and add to the weekly ops email.
